title: Developer Portfolio
summary: My portfolio and 30-day challenge log, built with React and Tailwind, with a Git-based CMS so I can publish a new project from a form in minutes.
body:
## What it does

This site is my portfolio and the live log of my 30-day challenge: 30 projects in 30 days, from React fundamentals to full-stack AI apps. The grid on the home page shows each day's progress, and every project has its own page with a write-up, the tech I used, and links to the live site and code.

## How I built it

The site is a React single-page app built with Vite, styled with Tailwind CSS, and routed with React Router. I kept content and code separate: every project is a JSON file, and the site loads them all at build time with Vite's import.meta.glob, so adding a project never means touching a component. Stats like the shipped count and the category filters are calculated from that data, so they can't go out of date.

To make updating easy, I added Sveltia CMS at /admin. It gives me a form for each project and commits my changes straight to GitHub, which triggers Vercel to rebuild and deploy the site in about a minute. There's no server or database to maintain: GitHub stores the content and Vercel serves it.

## What I learned

- How a React app reaches the screen: from one empty HTML page, through main.jsx and the router, down to each page and its components.
- useEffect must return nothing or a clean-up function. A one-line arrow function returned a value by accident and blanked the whole page with "destroy is not a function". Giving the effect a { } body fixed it.
- Single-page apps need a rewrite rule on the host. Without vercel.json, refreshing a project page gave a 404, because only one real HTML file exists.
- Git-based tools need a real Git repository. The CMS's local mode only worked after I ran git init, and signing in on the live site needed a fine-grained GitHub token with read and write access to Contents.
